data: Found together with a number of tombs, within the confines of the vineyard of the Signori Tumborello near Capo Boeo and reported by Salinas in NSA 1905

The archaeological collection is housed in one long room that has been subdivided into 4 discrete areas containing 25 cases and a series of open displays. 1 case contains pre- and proto-historic material, 3 are for material from Selinunte, 1 Camarina, 8 Erice, 1 Mozia, 1 Birgi, 1 Lilybaeum, 1 Centuripe, 4 contain material of unknown origin, 1 mixed sites, and then 1 for Punic stamped amphora handles, 1 for Greek and Roman stamped amphora handles, and 1 for Latin epigraphy. In addition there are open displays of material found on the seabed (amphorae, anchor parts, a Roman ram from the Aegadi Islands battle), a large two-sided Latin inscription and a section on Arabic and later Jewish inscriptions

Apparatus criticus

  • Text based upon photograph in Wilson

translation

Life to the (family of the) Pompeiani! On account of his distinguished justice, and of his literary merits, and of the love which he placed not only on his fatherland but on the whole province; to Iulius Claudius Peristerius Pompeianus, of clarissimus rank, former governor (consularis) of the province of Sicily; the whole council (curia), in a splendid meeting, set up this statue to its worthy and most excellent patron. Life to the (family of the) Amazonii! [translation from LSA 2853]

commentary

This inscription is on the reverse of the block employed for ISic000627, a prior, late C2 CE, honorific text.
